# ML Fundamentals Deep Dive (AI/ML & MLE Roles)

[← Google](../README.md) · [Every Google question](../../google.md) · [Read it on TrueInterview](https://trueinterview.io/study/ml-fundamentals-deep-dive)

`deep-dive` `ml-knowledge` `rag` `retrieval` `transformer`

---

## Requirements

This stage takes the form of an oral Q&A with a small amount of whiteboard derivation. Applicants choose a track during scheduling, and the interviewer adapts the discussion to it while keeping ML fundamentals as the foundation.

**Core ML fundamentals (covered in most loops)**

- Bias–variance tradeoff; ways to identify and reduce both.
- Overfitting and underfitting; practical fixes for each.
- Logistic regression: objective function, training procedure, and decision boundary.
- Gradient-descent forms: batch, mini-batch, SGD, momentum, and Adam — when each is appropriate.
- Cross-entropy: derive it and explain why classification usually favors it over MSE.
- L1 versus L2 regularization: how they differ, why L1 creates sparse weights (including the geometric reason), and why L2 behaves more smoothly.
- Forward and backward propagation: trace the chain rule, gradient movement, and parameter adjustment.
- Bayesian and frequentist viewpoints; likelihood; perplexity.
- Why Transformers outperform RNNs; attention complexity compared with a recurrent step; the expense of autoregressive generation.

**LLM / NLP track**

- Additional L4 AI/ML rounds may emphasize post-training, fine-tuning, prompt design, and the underlying Transformer machinery.
- Fine-tuning approaches (full, LoRA, adapters, and prefix); advantages and drawbacks of each.
- Inference topics: KV caching, top-p, top-k, nucleus sampling, and temperature sampling.
- Mixture-of-Experts designs.
- Compare tokenizers such as BPE, WordPiece, and SentencePiece.
- Generative AI: autoencoders, VAEs, and VQ-VAEs.
- Applying an LLM to product functionality (for example, recommendations driven by an LLM) — explain when retrieval is preferable to prompting and vice versa.

**Recsys track**

- Ways to address cold starts: content-based embeddings, collaborative filtering, and contextual bandits — present several alternatives rather than only one.
- Trade-offs between two-tower retrieval and ranking.
- Offline versus online measurement; counterfactual evaluation.
- LSH and ANN for large-scale retrieval; the relationship between embedding size and latency.
- Human-in-the-loop calibration for moderation false positives.

**CV track**

- ViTs versus CNNs; situations in which each performs better.
- Vector databases for similarity retrieval; product quantization.
- Quantization and pruning for serving systems at production scale.

**Project-dive sub-section** (~15 min)

- Choose a resume project and explain the problem definition, modeling decisions, reasons for rejecting alternatives, outcomes, and limitations.
- The interviewer looks for candor about failures and possible improvements — this provides the same Googliness signal as the BQ round.

## Notes

- You are expected to justify mechanisms, not merely name concepts. Saying “L1 creates sparsity” is insufficient — explain how the corners of the L1 ball drive weights to zero.
- Be prepared to derive the softmax plus cross-entropy gradient, the forward pass of attention, and gradient propagation through a residual block on a whiteboard.
- The interviewer might not have deep expertise in your chosen sub-track. One candidate reported that the interviewer matched keywords to a script instead of exploring specialized ideas. **State the conventional answer first**, followed by the more interesting modern version — do not open with niche papers.
- L4 AI/ML loops generally give project deep-dives more weight than textbook fundamentals; L5/L6 place greater emphasis on fundamentals and architectural trade-offs.
- Cross-checking: research-scientist (RS) loops include 2–5 separate research rounds (a talk plus 1-on-1 deep-dives), whereas MLE loops fold research into this one ML round.

## Preparation

- Work through and practice the *3 Blue 1 Brown* deep-learning and linear-algebra series for geometric intuition (L1/L2 balls and gradient fields).
- Handwrite the attention forward pass and the softmax and cross-entropy gradients at least three times, until the process is automatic.
- For the LLM track, read the Anthropic and OpenAI documentation on fine-tuning, KV caches, and sampling; commit the top-p, top-k, and temperature trade-off table to memory.
- For the Recsys track, study the TIGER, two-tower, and FAISS literature; prepare a paragraph on cold starts that combines collaborative filtering with content embeddings.
- For the CV track, practice ViT-versus-CNN trade-offs and study one quantization paper deeply enough to discuss it at a whiteboard.
- Keep 1–2 personal projects prepared for a deep-dive, and practice explaining why you selected each method instead of two alternatives.
